long_biography.plain_text:
Trained in aeronautical and missile engineering, Gismondi initially imagined manufacturing missile components. Their cost redirected him toward lighting, where a partnership with architect Sergio Mazza became Artemide. He brought engineering discipline to product development while commissioning leading architects and designers, turning research, manufacturing and creative collaboration into one operating model.

Gismondi also designed products himself and helped establish Memphis, the radical Milanese movement that challenged functionalist restraint with colour and geometric experimentation. At Artemide, he later articulated “The Human Light,” putting human needs at the centre of illumination and technological research. The company's international growth, museum-recognised products and Compasso d'Oro awards made his work a lasting part of Italian industrial design.
